clue.text: Caught by traffic light in curve of road

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
amber is the middle colour on a traffic light

explanation.surface: A driver gets stopped by a red-amber signal right on a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the slight convex slope given to a road surface so water drains off.

clue.text: Candour of author splitting one's sons

indicators.note: the author's word cuts the word for one's apart, sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: one's written without its apostrophe
a pen stands for a writer, as in pen-name
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son(s)

explanation.surface: An author's frankness is supposedly causing a rift between their boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour and openness are synonyms: both mean frankness and honesty in speech.

clue.text: I'd a chicory — mostly translated thus?

definitions.text: I'd a chicory — mostly translated thus?

indicators.note: translated means the letters are converted into a different form, rearranged
mostly means the word chicory loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks if this is what 'I had a chicory' becomes in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the Y of chicory, leaving CHICOR; with I'D and A that gives the letters to rearrange. The whole clue is the definition too, since radicchio is the Italian name for a red-leaved chicory.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is an Italian variety of chicory, so it is literally chicory rendered in Italian.

clue.text: Demonstrate for Leave, abandoning the European area

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: abandoning means the following letters are left out of the word Leave

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the, a European language's version of the word

explanation.surface: A Brexit-referendum campaign moment: show your support for Leave by quitting the EU zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a Brexit reading, but 'Leave' is a word to be cut down; 'the European' is a European language's word for 'the', French here.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove something is to demonstrate that it is true, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Call in auto for repairs after miscellaneous computer error?

indicators.note: after places the anagrammed part behind the abbreviation

parts.note: misc. is the usual abbreviation for miscellaneous

indicators.note: a car in for repairs is being fixed and reassembled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garage instruction: bring the car in for repairs following a computer fault.
explanation.walkthrough: MISC is followed by the anagram of CALLINAUTO, ALCULATION. The question mark flags that the definition is playful: an error made while computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscalculation is a mistake in working something out, an error in computing a figure.

clue.text: Small pepper is something seen as health food

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to pepper someone with missiles is to pelt them

explanation.surface: A dash of pepper is being promoted as good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pepper' looks like a seasoning noun but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is an ancient wheat species sold in health-food shops as a wholesome grain.

clue.text: Likeable fool at current company

parts.note: a simp is a simpleton, a fool
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A pleasant but foolish person is employed at a present-day firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico, borrowed from Italian and Spanish, means pleasant, congenial and easy to get on with.

clue.text: Little Tommy, perhaps a volunteer in the States

parts.note: minute means tiny, little
a Tommy is a British private soldier, an example of a man in military slang

explanation.surface: A small boy named Tommy might be a US volunteer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the traditional nickname for an ordinary British soldier, and 'man' is the term for a soldier in the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutemen were American colonial militia volunteers ready to fight at a minute's notice.

clue.text: Measure oxygen lost by body in space

indicators.note: lost by says the element's symbol drops out of the celestial body

parts.note: a meteor is a body travelling through space
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An astronomer gauges how much oxygen a celestial body has given off.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is a measuring instrument, and the word also serves as US spelling for the unit of length.

clue.text: Sight panorama, a moving and fantastic vision

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweeping panorama is both stirring and dreamlike to behold.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantasmagoria is a shifting sequence of dreamlike, illusory images, a fantastic vision.

clue.text: One changing position needs motorway finished

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a motorway, as in the M1
over means ended, finished

explanation.surface: Someone relocating needs the motorway roadworks to be completed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mover is anything or anyone that moves, so it changes its position.

clue.text: Awareness of judge's verdict about one

indicators.note: about means the verdict's letters go around the numeral

parts.note: a sentence is the punishment a judge pronounces
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the awareness shown in a judge's ruling on one defendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, which is a basic form of consciousness.

clue.text: Gone fishing? Letting one go is awkward

indicators.note: letting a thing go means releasing it, so the circle-shaped numeral is dropped
the second word of letting go: the numeral is released from the phrase

parts.note: taken as GO, as in to go fishing
O resembles the numeral for one
angling is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fisherman who keeps letting the catch slip off looks clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone fishing' reads as the sign on a closed shop, but it is GO ANGLING. 'Letting ... go' removes O (one), giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone tall, thin and loose-limbed, hence clumsy and ungainly in movement.

clue.text: Compliance requires Anglo-Saxon put into the post

parts.note: a letter put into the post has been sent

explanation.surface: Getting agreement means posting an Old English document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' looks like an insertion signal, but it belongs with 'the post' as a single phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is agreement or consent, which amounts to complying with a request.

clue.text: Check fluid room on top of any nuclear structure

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier part sits on top of the next

parts.note: ch. is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed in shape, so the letters flow into a new order

parts.note: some means any, as in have you some?

explanation.surface: An inspector checks an adjustable room atop some nuclear facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A chromosome is a thread of DNA found in the nucleus of a cell, a structure of the nucleus.

clue.text: Gold-gathering ruler buried in pyramid astonishes

indicators.note: buried in means the name lies concealed inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A greedy pharaoh's hoard entombed in a pyramid amazes onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth King Midas turned everything he touched into gold.

clue.text: Take pressure off leaning entrance

indicators.note: take ... off means remove, so the letter for pressure is removed
completes the phrase take off, telling us to remove a letter

parts.note: a penchant is a liking or leaning towards something
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Ease the strain on a door that is tilting at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway noun but is the verb en-TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone, stressed on the second syllable, is to captivate or bewitch them.

clue.text: Navy's front line cruise around stealthily

parts.note: the prow is the front of a ship, of which a navy is made

explanation.surface: A warship's leading edge slips quietly round on patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move about stealthily as if hunting, often cruising an area.

clue.text: Oil hot cooking vessel, turning that endlessly

indicators.note: turning means the cooking vessel is read backwards

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: endlessly means the word that loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Hot oil in a pan needs stirring, someone instructs.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts come in a different order from the clue: NAP, then H, then THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable liquid hydrocarbon mixture distilled from petroleum, a kind of oil.

clue.text: Mill — perhaps a new setting for one sitcom

indicators.note: giving words a new setting rearranges them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A TV producer moves a sitcom to a new location: an old mill.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stuart Mill, the Victorian philosopher, wrote Principles of Political Economy; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill was a political economist, an example of someone who studies economics.

clue.text: Shilling he had given away

parts.note: s. was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
he had contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: A man donated the shilling he owned.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to cast it off or discard it, so shed means got rid of.

clue.text: Help to find errors in score after hearing how Bohemian Rhapsody sounds?

indicators.note: after places the total behind the sound-alike word
hearing how a word sounds means we take its pronunciation, not its spelling
completes the instruction to go by the sound of the word

parts.note: Bohemia is the western region of the Czech Republic, so a Bohemian is Czech
a sum is a score in the sense of a total

explanation.surface: A music critic weighs Queen's Bohemian Rhapsody by ear and grades it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohemian Rhapsody is Queen's hit song; only 'Bohemian' gives letters. CZECH said aloud is CHECK.
explanation.definitionFit: A checksum is a figure computed from data so transmission errors can be detected.

clue.text: Title given to us in explosive series of contests

indicators.note: in means the phrase sits within the explosive's letters

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
something given to us is ours, our
a name is a title one goes by

explanation.surface: A grand title has been bestowed on us within a dramatic chain of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a competition made up of a series of matches or bouts.

clue.text: European kestrel dropping both wings over northern Dutch city

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier parts sit over the next
the bird's wings are its outermost letters, both of which are removed

parts.note: windhover is an old name for the kestrel, from its hovering

explanation.surface: A continental kestrel clips both wings while flying over a northern Netherlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: The windhover is the kestrel, famous from Hopkins's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a city in the southern Netherlands, home of Philips and PSV.

clue.text: What aids recall of witty remark about presiding spirit

indicators.note: about means the remark's letters are placed around the spirit

parts.note: a mot is a witty saying, from French bon mot
a numen is a divine power or spirit presiding over a place

explanation.surface: A quip concerns a guardian spirit that jogs the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is erected to commemorate, keeping a person or event in people's memory.

clue.text: Incline to get angry having dropped key climbing aid

parts.note: to tend is to incline towards something

indicators.note: having dropped means the musical letter falls out of the verb

parts.note: to rile is to anger, to get someone angry
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Someone prone to tantrums loses their keys and needs a hand climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender thread by which a climbing plant clings to its support.

clue.text: Daft person has alcohol served in cups

indicators.note: served in means the drink is placed inside the vessels

parts.note: mugs are large drinking cups
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A fool drinks his liquor out of teacups.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is British slang for a foolish person, often oneself, who gets put upon.

clue.text: Crime succeeded in opponent of King John being beheaded

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the shortened opponent
being beheaded means the noble loses his first letter

parts.note: the barons opposed King John and forced Magna Carta on him
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A crime was achieved when King John's enemy was executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being beheaded' cuts BARON to ARON, with S put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Variety of citrus fruit, not round

indicators.note: not means the round letter is left out of the fruit

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A type of citrus fruit is described as not spherical.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a variety or assortment, as in a wide range of goods.

clue.text: Look out for gloom's returning in this

definitions.text: Look out for gloom's returning in this

indicators.note: returning means the remaining letters are read backwards
out means the exclamation is taken out of the word gloom's

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A warning to watch for gloomy conditions coming back in this weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes the exclamation out of gloom's and 'returning' turns what is left round to give GOMS reversed. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: gloom comes back in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is a dense polluted fog that brings murky, gloomy conditions.
